message.content: {"thought": "The FFN group dominates: 234.3B latency sum (vs 82.8B for attention), with 100% of FFN time in compute (calc_time = 234.3B). The FFN group has 32 layers (16 FFN1 tilings + 16 FFN2 tilings) with 64 occurrences. The FFN1 tilings each have ~14.5B latency, so 16 FFN1 tilings contribute ~232B of the 234.3B FFN latency. This confirms that increasing compute units per chiplet from 4096 to 16384 would directly reduce the dominant FFN1 latency by ~4x, from ~232B to ~58B, potentially reducing total latency from 71.3B to ~(71.3 - 232*0.75) = ~(71.3 - 174) = negative, which doesn't make sense because the timeline shows critical path is ~29.1B, not the sum. The critical path is the max across cores, not the sum. The FFN1 tilings are parallelized across 16 chiplets via tensor_parall=16, so each chiplet processes one tiling. The critical path includes one FFN1 tiling (~14.5B) plus FFN2 and other layers. Increasing compute_units to 16384 would reduce each FFN1 tiling from ~14.5B to ~3.6B, reducing critical path latency significantly. However, this would increase monetary cost. Let me check the hardware config and then consider the tradeoff. I'll also look at historical cases if any exist.", "action": "tool", "tool": {"name": "summarize_hardware_config", "arguments": {"include_design_space": true}}}
